ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The cell lineage labeled “Wild-type” on the left side of the figure continues to divide upward, and the radiolabeled cells continue to produce more progeny; the lineage labeled “Mutant” on the right side stops after dividing into two cells, with “No further replication” clearly marked next to it. Reasoning: The experiment text states that the temperature-sensitive cdc mutant cannot re-enter interphase after mitosis at 37°C. If the mutant is placed at 37°C from the beginning, that is, first exposed to the restrictive temperature, it will arrest before continuing to establish growth; then switching to 25°C afterward, according to the description of this experiment, also will not allow it to continue growing. Therefore the answer is negative.

raw_record.question_text: Based on the experiments described, if the cdc mutants were initially incubated at 37°C and then switched to 25°C, would the mutants grow? Answer yes or no.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the mutant lineage stops and is marked “No further replication,” while wild-type continues dividing. Then read the experiment text stating that temperature-sensitive cdc mutants grown at 37°C cannot re-enter interphase after mitosis. Apply this to the counterfactual: starting at 37°C exposes the mutants first to the restrictive condition, so they arrest before establishing growth. Therefore switching afterward to 25°C would not make them grow; answer no.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧标为“Wild-type”的细胞谱系持续向上分裂，放射标记后的细胞继续产生更多子代；右侧标为“Mutant”的谱系在分裂到两个细胞后停止，旁边明确标注“No further replication”。推理：实验文字说明，温度敏感型 cdc 突变体在 37°C 下不能在有丝分裂后重新进入间期。若突变体一开始就被置于 37°C，即先暴露在限制性温度下，它们会在继续建立生长前发生停滞；之后再切换到 25°C，依据该实验描述也不会使其继续生长。因此答案是否定的。

method.method_draft: First describe the image: wild-type cells show repeated divisions, but mutant cells stop after the labeled division stage with no further replication. Then use Experiment 2’s text: cdc mutants initially incubated at 25°C for 30 minutes completed several rounds of mitosis before later exposure near 37°C arrested them. The question reverses this order, putting mutants at 37°C first. Since 37°C is the arresting condition and the permissive 25°C period did not occur first, the mutants would not grow. Answer no.
